title: Enforcer key-namespace mismatch allows transient bypass of per-key quotas
creator: Maya Chen
description: Production reports surfaced a pattern where org-level and route-level rate limits were incorrectly attributed when requests traverse alias routes and proxy rewrite layers. The policy enforcer normalizes enforcement keys using a namespace derived from route metadata; when route-alias rewriting happens mid-flight (edge proxy + internal router), the enforcer occasionally uses the pre-rewrite namespace to record token consumption while enforcing against the post-rewrite policy. This leads to transient mismatches where per-key counters are incremented on the wrong logical key/shard, producing both silent under-enforcement (clients not throttled despite exceeding quotas) and underbilling for affected tenant requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two routes R1 and R2 that share a backend but have distinct policy namespaces (org-scoped quota on R1, route-scoped quota on R2).
2) Configure an edge alias that rewrites requests from R1 -> R2 for A/B deploys (header-based rewrite + internal route alias).
3) Generate high qps traffic with mixed keys (same API key used on both logical routes).

4) Observe that the usage counter increments are recorded under the pre-rewrite namespace in Redis (via trace logs) while enforcement queries use the post-rewrite namespace, creating a temporary gap where enforcement allows extra tokens.
5) Reproduce more reliably by introducing a small artificial delay on the route-bind metadata refresh path to widen the race window.
investigation_notes: Initial alerts originated from billing-heartbeat dashboard (billing-ops) showing token delta mismatch across shards for org 'acme-inc' starting 2026-02-17.
Correlation between increased traffic during a deployment and gaps in enforcement suggests a race between route-alias metadata propagation and enforcer cache invalidation.

Trace sample 2026-02-19T18:12Z shows request flow: edge -> alias rewrite -> internal router -> enforcer: key_namespace used in increment != key_namespace used in allowance check (diff by 1 byte on namespace suffix).

Reproducer run with local redis emulator confirmed that non-atomic read/construct/increment path is root cause: enforcer performs separate key construction and allowance lookup across async cache refresh callbacks.

Sharding logic assigns counters by namespace hash; when different namespaces are used for lookup vs increment, counters are written to different shards leading to undercounting of consumed tokens in enforcement decisions.
No data corruption observed in underlying Redis cluster, but accounting divergence persists until reconciliation runs.
mitigation: Hotfix enforcer patch to centralize key normalization and perform allowance check + increment in a single atomic Lua script when possible; temporary config flip to stricter deny-on-ambiguous-mapping for high-risk orgs; immediate reconciliation job to scan recent traces and backfill missing increments for billing accuracy.
temporary_workarounds: 1) Feature-flagged enforcement_mode=strict for customers with suspected divergence (blocks requests when ambiguity detected).
2) Disable edge alias route rewrites for impacted customers until release can be rolled (applied selectively to a handful of enterprise tenants).
3) Scoped rate-limiter sampling increase to surface mismatches earlier in dashboards.
playbook_runbook_notes: Pager alerted on 2026-02-18 03:14 UTC; initial triage team: Maya, Arjun, Samir (on-call infra).
Triage conclusion: production safety risk due to silent quota bypass. Prioritize P0 remediation and billing reconciliation.

Action taken: enabled strict enforcement_mode for two orgs, launched reconciliation job to backfill token increments for the last 48 hours, and scheduled a canary rollout of enforcer patch to staging -> prod-small -> prod-wide.
Communications: Notified billing-ops, customer-success, and impacted customers; CS outreach drafted to explain reconciliation and any invoice adjustments.
next_steps: 1) Merge and ship enforcer PR with atomic allowance+increment (owner: Arjun).
2) Roll canary to prod-small, monitor 'usage-delta' and 'throttle-events' dashboards for 48h.
3) Run reconciliation to backfill counters and prepare provisional invoice corrections (billing-ops).
4) Harden test-suite with synthetic alias-rewrite scenarios and add e2e test that asserts namespace consistency across proxy rewrites.
5) Postmortem and customer-facing notes to be published after stabilization.
notes_for_release: runtime-1.21 will include enforcer atomic key normalization and a migration job. Release notes should call out: fixed race in quota attribution when using route aliases/proxy rewrites; improved accounting integrity; no data loss expected but reconciliation applied for affected windows.
qa_plan: Create deterministic e2e harness that simulates edge rewrite + internal router path with controllable timing; assert allowance+increment atomicity across race windows; run regression suite against older enforcer builds to ensure no behavioral regressions.
engineer_comments: Arjun: Implemented Lua script to perform allow-check and conditional increment in a single shard transaction. Local benchmarks show additional 2ms p99 on enforcement path but eliminates mismatch window.
Maya: Billing-ops wants reconciliation details; we'll provide backfill summaries and list of affected orgs.
Samir: Consider increasing route metadata TTL to reduce cache churn; separate follow-up ticket proposed.
